question: Ben's hens gave him 232 eggs this week. His neighbour Ana, whose hens laid fewer eggs than Ben's, gave him 52 eggs, and he bought 55 more from a farm shop. His stall is 3 metres wide. Ben sold every egg for 7 cents. He then spent 2352 cents on chicken feed. How many cents did Ben have left?

A hotel counts its pillows one by one rather than by the room. On Monday morning the linen store held 91 pillows, and a delivery added 80 before lunch. In the afternoon 84 pillows were taken up to the new rooms. That evening the manager ordered enough for the store to hold 4 times as many pillows as were left. On Tuesday a guest room returned 9 pillows to the store. How many pillows are in the linen store now?

A candy shop had 67 pounds of gummy bears in the bulk bin. A morning sale used up 6 pounds. A big restock added 42 more pounds. A dozen new candy jars were added to the shelf, though that number has nothing to do with the gummy bear weight. The shop then repackaged the bin into individual 8-ounce bags, multiplying the tracked count by 8 to get the total number of bags. A late delivery added 5 more bags to the tracked count. Finally, a wholesale order multiplied the tracked bag count by 8. A separate bin of sour worms, unrelated to this count, held 90 pounds. How many bags did the tracked count come to?

Tom started with 156 dollars. He multiplied his money by 9 when he received his paycheck bonus. He then added 37 dollars from a refund. He received another 18 dollars from a friend. He got 30 dollars as a birthday gift. Finally, he spent 152 dollars on electronics. How much money did Tom have at the end?

Lars keeps 115 sheets of plywood in his workshop, and a supplier delivered 72 more. A kitchen job used 161 sheets, and a small repair used 9 more. A neighbour then returned 46 sheets that were the wrong size, and an auction added 24 sheets to the pile. Each sheet in the workshop can be cut into 7 shelves. Lars holds more plywood than his colleague Ida does, and his van is 5 metres long. How many shelves can Lars cut?

A driving school had 163 lesson slots booked for the month. 86 slots were used in the first week and 27 in the second. Bad weather forced 47 slots to be cancelled altogether. A new instructor then added 59 slots to the diary. Every slot still in the diary needs 8 pages of paperwork. The office records lesson lengths in minutes even though the invoices to learners quote hours. How many pages of paperwork does the diary require?
A project had 52 items. They added 77, reaching 129. They doubled to 258. They multiplied by 9 to 2,322. They removed 293, leaving 2,029. They tripled to 6,087 items. How many items total?

A container started with 17 liters of liquid. Production multiplied by 6 (102 liters). Processing halved the volume (51 liters). Consumption removed 4 liters (47 liters). Refilling added 55 liters (102 liters). A final batch added 11 liters (113 liters). End-of-day closing removed 44 liters. Converting to gallons, this represented about 18.2 gallons. How many liters remained?

A warehouse started with 185 boxes. They removed 140 boxes. They removed 22 more boxes. They removed another 22 boxes. Their remaining inventory increased 4 times. A competing warehouse had 400 boxes. How many boxes does this warehouse have?

On Friday morning a food bank's shelf held 112 tins of soup. Volunteers took 34 tins out for the breakfast run, and a supermarket delivered 46 tins before noon. In the early afternoon a matching-gift scheme doubled the number of tins on the shelf. Later that afternoon the stock was divided equally between the charity's 4 branches, and the tins staying at the main branch are the ones being followed. In the evening 51 tins were handed out at the main branch's door. The rota is written in hours although volunteers record their shifts in minutes. How many tins are left at the main branch?
Two managers tracked progress. One had 34 items initially. They doubled, multiplied by 5, added 59, removed 52, and multiplied by 8. How many items?

A community garden plot had 40 tomato plants at the start of spring. Volunteers added 15 more seedlings in early April. A donation from a local nursery brought in 65 additional plants in May. By June, the garden had grown by 32 more plants thanks to a seed-sharing event. When the harvest was divided evenly among 4 neighborhood families, only one family's share continued to be tracked for the community log. That family then lost 6 plants to a late blight. How many tomato plants did that family end up with?

A company started with 199 units. Their revenue increased 7 times in the morning. By afternoon, they spent 510 units. By evening, they spent 844 more units. Their remaining resources increased 9 times. Finally, they tripled. Converting to hundreds, how many units do they have?

In the morning a lemonade stand had 85 cups ready, and the owner made 53 more. 7 cups were knocked over and spilled. In the afternoon every cup was sold for 7 cents. In the evening a customer came back and left a 25-cent tip. How many cents did the stand take in?

A library had 202 books initially. They added 77 books from donation. They multiplied by 6 for the catalog value. They added 77 books from purchase. They removed 824 books for archive (in dollars). They multiplied by 6 for insurance calculation. How many dollars was the insurance value?

A lemonade stand's tank held 46 gallons at opening, and the owners poured in 70 more gallons before the crowd arrived. They serve by the cup, so they worked out the volume in cups: there are 4 quarts in a gallon, and 4 cups in a quart. During the day they served 706 cups. How many cups of lemonade are left in the tank?

A bakery had 233 items. They added 20 items from morning prep. They multiplied by 5 for the daily batch. They added 37 items from afternoon bake. They added 52 items from the delivery. How many items were in inventory?

A bead workshop began with 94 tubs of beads. Each tub was emptied into 3 jars, and every jar was tipped into 2 pouches. The pouches were shared equally among the workshop's 3 tables, and the tutor sat at one of them. Each pouch on the tutor's table was opened into 2 dishes, and every dish holds 4 beads. A child then dropped 4 loose beads onto that table. The workshop lasts 90 minutes. How many beads are on the tutor's table?

A company starts with 161 items. It multiplies by 3 (483). It multiplies by 2 (966). It adds 71 (1037). It loses 304 (733). It loses 23 (710). It loses 479. Morning to afternoon to evening progression. Time measured in minutes to hours. How many items remain?

A toy factory employed 232 workers and hired 77 more for the holiday rush. Every worker assembles 9 toy cars an hour and works a 5-hour shift each day, three hundred minutes as the notice board puts it. The factory floor has 3 assembly lines. The workers kept this up for 7 days, and a trial batch added 71 more cars. Quality control then rejected 22427 cars. How many cars passed quality control?

Petra had 111 chocolates in a box for the office and found 5 more loose in her bag. Her colleague Denis, who had brought none of his own, handed 79 of them round at the morning meeting. Another 34 went out with the afternoon tea. Petra ate 2 herself before going home. How many chocolates are left in the box?

A single lemonade stand cash box started the morning with 44 dollars. In the morning, 24 more dollars came in from early customers. In the afternoon, 28 dollars were spent restocking cups and lemons. Later that afternoon, 16 more dollars came in, after a rush that lasted about 30 minutes, roughly half an hour. That evening, 20 more dollars came in from a final wave of customers. How much money was in the cash box by the end of the evening?

Kenji stacked 9 boxes with 169 tiles in each box. Every tile in the yard is scored into 3 smaller squares. A builder then carried off 1104 squares, more than Kenji's helper Mei had ever moved in a day. Mei added 54 squares she found on an old pallet. Half of the yard is under cover. How many squares are in the yard?

A warehouse started with 95 items. They multiplied by 9 for inventory assessment. They subtracted 438 items fulfilled. They added 54 items from new delivery. Finally, 114 items were deducted for returns. Using the word 'half', between Steven (morning) and Nicole (evening), how many items are managed?

Kit had 61 cents in her money box. She added 71 cents that she found in the car and then 50 cents from her grandfather. Her brother paid back 49 cents he had borrowed. She then spent 224 cents on a comic book. Kit prefers to write her savings in dollars, since a hundred cents make one dollar. How many cents are in her money box now?
